'''Tsugawa Shrine''' (積川神社) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|en|Shinto shrine|qid=Q845945|lt=Shinto shrine}} located in Tsugawa Town, [[Kishiwada City]], {{ill|Osaka Prefecture|en|Osaka Prefecture|qid=Q122723|lt=Osaka Prefecture}}, Japan. It is an {{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|abstract|Q11064932|fr|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|ja|延喜式神名帳|simple|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|zh|延喜式神名帳|qid=Q11064932|lt=Shikinaisha}} and formerly held the Rank of [[Gōsha]]. It is considered the Fourth Shrine of {{ill|Izumi Province|en|Izumi Province|qid=Q1047117|lt=Izumi Province}} and was an imperial prayer site.

== Deities ==
* Main Deities - Ikui-no-Kami, Sakui-no-Kami, Tsunagai-no-Kami, Asuha-no-Kami, Hahiki-no-Kami.

These deities are collectively known as the {{ill|Ikasuri no Kami|ja|座摩神|zh|坐摩巫祭神|qid=Q10928586}}.

== History ==
The shrine is said to have been established during the reign of Emperor Sujin and is recorded in the ''[[Engishiki]]'' compiled in 927.

In 864, it was Ranked Junior Fourth Rank, Lower Grade, and elevated to Junior Fourth Rank, Upper Grade in 873.

According to shrine legend, in 1090, Emperor Shirakawa visited Kumano and wrote the shrine’s plaque himself, replacing an earlier one with poor calligraphy.

The shrine received various imperial patronages and was linked to important historical events, including land grants and restorations ordered by figures like Toyotomi Hideyori in 1603.

It became a [[Gōsha]] in 1873 and was designated an Important Cultural Property in 1950.

== {{ill|Haisho|ja|拝所|qid=Q17194083|lt=Worship Site}} ==
The Tsugawa Shrine {{ill|Haisho|ja|拝所|qid=Q17194083|lt=worship site}} is located along the [[Kumano Kodō|Kumano Kodo]] route in Komatsusato Town, allowing distant parishioners to worship.

== Grounds ==
* Main Hall (Important Cultural Property) - Renovated in 1603 by Toyotomi Hideyori.
* Stone Lanterns - Donated by Kusunoki Masanori.
* Middle Gate
* Worship Hall
* Shrine Office
* Tsugawa Town Shrine Hall
* External Sites
** {{ill|Haisho|ja|拝所|qid=Q17194083|lt=Worship Site}} (Otabisho)

== Cultural Properties ==
=== Important Cultural Property ===
* Main Hall - Designated in 1914.

=== Osaka Prefecture Designated Cultural Properties ===
* Wooden Male and Female deity Statues - Kamakura Period.
* Plaque - Inscribed by Emperor Shirakawa in 1090.

=== Kishiwada City Designated Natural Monuments ===
* Mukuro Tree

=== Others ===
* Portable Shrine - Believed to be dedicated by Yodogimi.
* Ancient Mirror
